<h1 class="article-title">References</h1>
<p class="standfirst">Every dataset and publication behind this project</p>

::: {.refs}
1. **[U.S. Department of Education, College Scorecard](https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/).** Most Recent Cohorts institution file and historical archive (1996-97 to 2025-26), June 2026 release. Washington, DC: U.S. Department of Education, Office of Planning, Evaluation and Policy Development. [Data documentation](https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/data/)

   Institution-level cost, aid, enrollment, completion, debt and post-enrollment earnings for nearly every degree-granting institution in the United States. Used for the cross-sectional analysis (sticker price, net price by income bracket, debt, earnings and the earnings regression) and, via the historical archive, the 25-year tuition trend.

2. **[Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis (FRED) / U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CPIAUCSL).** Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items in U.S. City Average (CPIAUCSL), seasonally adjusted, monthly.

   Converts nominal dollar figures from different years into constant 2025 dollars, so tuition and cost figures from different academic years compare on an inflation-adjusted basis.

3. **[Chetty, Raj, John N. Friedman, Emmanuel Saez, Nicholas Turner and Danny Yagan. "Mobility Report Cards: The Role of Colleges in Intergenerational Mobility."](https://www.nber.org/papers/w23618)** NBER Working Paper No. 23618, 2017. [Opportunity Insights paper page](https://opportunityinsights.org/paper/mrc/).

   An independent analysis built on de-identified federal tax and enrollment records rather than institution-reported averages, covering the family-income distribution and post-college outcomes of students at "Ivy-Plus" colleges, a group that includes Stanford. Cited for context on who enrolls at elite private universities; its microdata is not publicly downloadable and is not part of this project's analysis universe.
:::

## How these sources relate to the data pipeline

`scripts/download.py` fetches sources 1 and 2 programmatically; both are public and machine-readable. Source 3 is cited for context and is not pulled into the pipeline.

Full data-cleaning and modeling detail: [Methods](methods.qmd).
